name:        useTableSortableState
domain:      hook
package:     @astryxdesign/core
import:      @astryxdesign/core/Table
description: Owns a Table's sort state and sorts the rows locally, as a convenience layer over useTableSortable. Pass the rows in, render sortedData, and hand sortConfig to useTableSortable. The hook keeps the state (or reads it from sort and onSortChange when controlled), so header clicks re-sort the rows with no sort code in the component. With isMultiSortEnabled, Shift+click adds tiebreaker columns. For data sorted on a server, use useTableSortable directly and sort where the data lives.
command:     npx @astryxdesign/cli@0.7.12 hook useTableSortableState

name:        useCalendarDays
domain:      hook
package:     @astryxdesign/core
import:      @astryxdesign/core/Calendar
description: Builds the day grid for one month: every date to show, including the previous and next months' days that fill the first and last weeks, grouped into weeks, plus localized weekday header names that start on weekStartsOn. It is the layout Calendar uses, for a custom month view such as a compact availability grid or a mini calendar. It returns data only: rendering, selection, keyboard navigation and the grid's accessibility semantics are the caller's.
command:     npx @astryxdesign/cli@0.7.12 hook useCalendarDays

name:        useTableGroupedRows
domain:      hook
package:     @astryxdesign/core
import:      @astryxdesign/core/hooks
description: Hook that groups a flat data array into collapsible section rows. Each distinct groupBy value becomes a full-width section-header row with a chevron toggle, the group label, and a member count; collapsing hides that group's data rows while keeping the header visible. The disclosure state lives on the chevron button, not the native table row. Mirrors useTableTreeState: the consumer owns the collapsedGroups set and the hook returns {data, plugin, idKey}: pass them to Table as data, plugins, and idKey respectively. Grouping runs on the rows you hand it, so with pagination the order is filter, sort, slice, then group: sort by the group key first and the user's keys second, so a section's rows stay contiguous and each page appends to the bottom of the table instead of splicing rows in above the reader. A page that ends on a row count still cuts mid-section, and the heading then counts what has loaded rather than what exists: "6" quietly becoming "10". Where the full result set is in hand, carry the cut forward to the end of the section it lands in: every rendered section is then whole and its count is a total.
command:     npx @astryxdesign/cli@0.7.12 hook useTableGroupedRows

name:        useTableRowExpansion
domain:      hook
package:     @astryxdesign/core
import:      @astryxdesign/core/hooks
description: Hook that returns a TablePlugin which expands a full-width detail panel below a row, rendered by the consumer via renderExpanded(item). Adds a leading chevron column and a right-click "Expand/Collapse row" action; the consumer owns the expandedKeys set. The panel spans the row but starts its content at the first column, past the chevron, so detail lines up with the labels above it; the inset follows the table density. Use it for master-detail rows (order details, forms, charts, nested tables). For hierarchical data where child rows reuse the parent columns, use useTableTreeData + useTableTreeState instead.
command:     npx @astryxdesign/cli@0.7.12 hook useTableRowExpansion

name:        useTableRowIndex
domain:      hook
package:     @astryxdesign/core
import:      @astryxdesign/core/hooks
description: Hook that returns a TablePlugin which prepends a right-aligned, monospaced row-number column, starting at 1 by default. Without data, Table supplies row positions; with data, ordinary numbers follow that array. Windowed rows use the parent Table logical position directly; nondefault startFrom values use full rendering.
command:     npx @astryxdesign/cli@0.7.12 hook useTableRowIndex

name:        useTableRowsVirtualization
domain:      hook
package:     @astryxdesign/core
import:      @astryxdesign/core/hooks
description: Returns an opaque capability for fixed-height flat-row Table windowing. Pass the capability to Table.virtualization and keep the complete data, columns, explicit stable idKey and plugins on Table. Sizes are positive finite CSS pixels. Supported rows use single-line content; explicit wrapping, arbitrary custom renderers, non-flat rows or invalid identity use ordinary full rendering. Windowing uses the Table-owned scroll wrapper; a caller-provided scrollWrapper takes diagnostic full-render fallback. Mounted rows retain native table semantics and full-table positions; unmounted rows are not promised screen-reader discovery.
command:     npx @astryxdesign/cli@0.7.12 hook useTableRowsVirtualization

name:        useTableTreeData
domain:      hook
package:     @astryxdesign/core
import:      @astryxdesign/core/hooks
description: Headless tree plugin for Table: renders nested rows with per-level indentation and expand/collapse chevrons in the tree column (the first column by default), and reflects hierarchy with aria-level on body rows and aria-expanded on each expand/collapse button. Composable with the other Table plugins: the canonical plugin order places tree before selection, so the checkbox column lands left of the indented tree column. Feed it the treeConfig from useTableTreeState, or construct the config directly for server-driven or pre-flattened trees. When no row is expandable (flat data), every transform is a pass-through and the table renders identically to one without the plugin. Known limitation: the tree column wraps its cell content, so textOverflow="truncate" tooltips do not apply within the tree column.
command:     npx @astryxdesign/cli@0.7.12 hook useTableTreeData

name:        useTableTreeState
domain:      hook
package:     @astryxdesign/core
import:      @astryxdesign/core/hooks
description: State management companion for useTableTreeData. Owns the expanded set (controlled or uncontrolled) and flattens nested data into the visible row array; collapsed subtrees are unmounted, not hidden, so the table body contains exactly the visible rows. Returns expandAll/collapseAll helpers, the aggregate isAllExpanded state (true/false/indeterminate) for a header expand-all control, and a ready-to-use config for the tree plugin. Note: because collapsed rows unmount, cell-local React state inside collapsed subtrees is lost on collapse; lift state that must survive.
command:     npx @astryxdesign/cli@0.7.12 hook useTableTreeState

name:        useTableRowStatus
domain:      hook
package:     @astryxdesign/core
import:      @astryxdesign/core/hooks
description: Hook that returns a TablePlugin which prepends a narrow column signaling per-row status. Return {status, label} for a semantic success, warning, or error: Table resolves the matching glyph and tone through the active theme. Return {color, icon?, label} for a custom marker: every color is paint-only, an omitted icon renders the stable 8px dot, and an explicit icon renders that caller-selected glyph. Named custom icons keep their released Icon color mapping; raw CSS custom icons inherit the caller's exact paint instead of the previous primary fallback. Existing callers require no source migration. label is required and becomes the accessible image name plus supplemental hover tooltip; return null for no indicator. The column header is visually blank but carries a screen-reader-only localized name ("Row status", i18n key @astryx.table.rowStatus.columnHeader). Memoize getStatus with useCallback for a stable plugin identity.
command:     npx @astryxdesign/cli@0.7.12 hook useTableRowStatus

name:        createReorderable
domain:      hook
package:     @astryxdesign/core
import:      @astryxdesign/core
description: Makes a collection's rows reorderable. On a touch screen a finger held still on a row's handle for a moment picks it up (a flick on the handle still scrolls): the row stays in its place, dimmed, while a copy of it follows the finger and an accent line marks where it would land; the other rows stay still, the page scrolls near its edges, and on release the rows rearrange. A pen held still on a handle where the primary pointer is coarse picks the row up as a finger does. A mouse, or a pen where the primary pointer is fine, drags a handle at once the same way, and the rows take their places without motion; a cancelled drag puts everything back at once. Without a drag, the handle toggles reorder mode for its row (a click, Space or Enter): each arrow key moves the row a place at once, and Escape or another activation ends the mode, keeping the moves; screen readers hear each move with the row's place and neighbours, and a hint shows the moves and Done as buttons, for taps alone. The reorder code ships with this function: a collection without the prop loads none of it.
command:     npx @astryxdesign/cli@0.7.12 hook createReorderable
